questions.passage: Scientists studying asteroid deflection have focused on secondary objects such as S/2020 (2013 PY6), a moonlet orbiting the near-Earth asteroid 2013 PY6. In 2022 NASA intentionally crashed a probe into just such an object, the moonlet Dimorphos. __________ Dimorphos's orbital period around the near-Earth asteroid Didymos was permanently altered.
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is C, "Consequently," This is an Expression of Ideas question testing the Transitions skill, rated medium difficulty. The task is to choose the transition word that best fits the logical relationship between the sentence before the blank and the sentence containing the blank.

Core Concepts
A transition is a word or phrase that signals how two ideas relate. Each transition type expresses a specific relationship:

  • Cause/Effect (Consequently, Therefore, As a result): the second idea is the outcome or result of the first.
  • Contrast/Comparison (In comparison, However, By contrast): the second idea is set against or measured alongside the first.
  • Addition (In addition, Furthermore, Moreover): the second idea adds another separate, parallel point.
  • Specification (Specifically, In particular): the second idea narrows in to give a more precise detail about the first.

The strategy is to ignore the answer choices at first, read the two sentences, and decide the relationship yourself before matching it to a choice.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Sentence before the blank: "In 2022 NASA intentionally crashed a probe into just such an object, the moonlet Dimorphos." This states an action or event that was performed.
  • Sentence with the blank: "__________ Dimorphos's orbital period around the near-Earth asteroid Didymos was permanently altered." This states what happened to Dimorphos afterward.
  • Relationship: The crash is the cause; the permanently altered orbital period is the direct effect. Crashing a probe into the moonlet is precisely what changed its orbit.
  • Match: A cause-and-effect relationship calls for a result transition. "Consequently" means "as a result," which fits exactly.

Why Each Answer

  • A, "In comparison," (Incorrect — Wrong Relationship/Contrast): This signals that two things are being weighed against each other. The passage is not comparing two items; it is showing that one event produced an outcome.
  • B, "In addition," (Incorrect — Wrong Relationship/Addition): This signals a separate, additional fact. But the changed orbit is not a new, unrelated point; it is the direct result of the crash already described.
  • C, "Consequently," (Correct): This signals result. It correctly shows that the orbital period changed because NASA crashed the probe into the moonlet.
  • D, "Specifically," (Incorrect — Wrong Relationship/Specification): This signals that a narrower detail about the previous statement follows. The second sentence does not zoom in on the crash; it reports a new consequence of it.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For transition questions, cover the choices and predict the relationship in your own words first. Here, plugging in "As a result" makes the sentences read smoothly — a reliable sign the cause/effect transition ("Consequently") is correct. Watch for the tested trap where an effect is disguised as merely an "additional" fact (choice B).
questions.question_text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.passage: According to the free electron model, metals, such as copper and silver, do not maintain bonds by sharing and exchanging electrons. __________ metals are held together by a system of valence electrons that travel freely, interacting with neither ions nor each other. This framework for understanding the subatomic relationships within metals can be used to help explain heat and electrical conductivity.
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B, "Rather,". This is an Expression of Ideas question testing the Transitions skill at a medium difficulty level. Your job is to choose the transition word that correctly shows how the idea before the blank relates to the idea after it.

Core Concepts
A transition is a word or phrase that signals the logical relationship between two ideas. To pick the right one, you must first identify what kind of relationship exists between the sentences. The main families of transitions are:

  • Contrast / correction (rather, instead, however, on the contrary): used when the second idea corrects, replaces, or opposes the first.
  • Example (for example, for instance): used when the second idea is a specific illustration of the first.
  • Cause and effect (accordingly, therefore, as a result): used when the second idea is a consequence of the first.
  • Similarity / addition (likewise, similarly, also): used when the second idea is parallel to or agrees with the first.

The word "rather" specifically means "instead" or "on the contrary" and is used to replace a rejected idea with the true one, following a "not X, but instead Y" pattern.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Sentence 1 (before the blank): States a negative claim about metals: they "do not maintain bonds by sharing and exchanging electrons." This tells us what does NOT happen.
  • Sentence 2 (with the blank): States what DOES happen: metals "are held together by a system of valence electrons that travel freely." This is the true explanation that replaces the rejected one.
  • The relationship: The passage sets up a "not this, but instead this" structure. The second sentence corrects the picture by supplying the actual mechanism. A correction/contrast transition is required.
  • Match the transition: "Rather" precisely signals "instead / on the contrary," linking the rejected idea to the correct one.

Why Each Answer

  • A. "For example," — Trap: Wrong Relationship (Illustration). The second sentence is not a specific example of the first; it is the corrected explanation. Nothing in sentence 1 is being illustrated.
  • B. "Rather," (CORRECT) — It signals correction, replacing the rejected idea (not bonding by sharing electrons) with the true one (held together by freely traveling valence electrons), matching the "not X, instead Y" logic perfectly.
  • C. "Accordingly," — Trap: Wrong Relationship (Cause-Effect). "Accordingly" means "as a result," but the second sentence is not a consequence of the first; it is a contrasting correction.
  • D. "Likewise," — Trap: Wrong Relationship (Similarity). "Likewise" signals agreement or parallelism, but the two sentences contrast a negative claim with a positive one, so a similarity transition is the opposite of what is needed.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When a sentence tells you what something is NOT and the next sentence tells you what it actually IS, look for a correction transition like "rather" or "instead." A quick mental trigger: if you can paraphrase the two sentences as "not this, but instead that," the answer is almost always the contrast/correction word.
questions.question_text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

questions.passage: In an ekphrastic poem, a poet explores a work of visual art, such as a drawing, sculpture, or painting. Robert Hayden's 1994 poem "Monet's Waterlilies," for example, meditates on Claude Monet's 1899 painting Water Lilies; Saad Ali's 2020 poem "This Town," __________ takes a painting as its subject: Ivan Aivazovsky's 1859 work Lunar Night on the Black Sea.
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is (C) likewise,. This is an Expression of Ideas question testing the Transitions skill, at an easy difficulty level. The task is to choose the transition word that best fits the logical relationship between the two ideas joined at the blank.

Core Concepts
A transition word signals how one idea relates to another. Each type points in a different direction:

  • Addition / Similarity (likewise, similarly, also, in the same way): the second idea matches or parallels the first.
  • Contrast (nevertheless, however, conversely, on the other hand): the second idea opposes or surprises us after the first.
  • Cause and Effect (hence, therefore, thus, as a result): the first idea causes the second.
An ekphrastic poem is simply a poem that describes or responds to a piece of visual art (a painting, sculpture, or drawing). You do not need any prior knowledge of the poems or paintings named; the answer comes entirely from the structure of the sentence.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Sentence 1 (setup): Defines an ekphrastic poem as one that explores a work of visual art.
  • Clause before the blank: Gives one example. Robert Hayden's poem "Monet's Waterlilies" meditates on a Monet painting. This is an ekphrastic poem.
  • Clause after the blank: Gives a second example. Saad Ali's poem "This Town" takes a painting (Aivazovsky's work) as its subject. This is also an ekphrastic poem.
  • Relationship: Both clauses describe the SAME kind of thing: a poem built around a painting. The word "takes a painting as its subject" mirrors "meditates on... painting." The second example reinforces the first, so the connection is one of similarity.
  • Choose: A similarity transition is required, which points to "likewise."

Why Each Answer

  • (C) likewise, - Correct. It signals that the second poem behaves the same way as the first, both being ekphrastic poems about paintings. This matches the parallel structure exactly.
  • (A) nevertheless, - Contrast trap. It signals an unexpected reversal, but the second example simply agrees with and adds to the first. There is no contrast.
  • (B) conversely, - Contrast trap. It claims the second idea is the opposite of the first. Both poems do the same thing, so "opposite" is the reverse of the true relationship.
  • (D) hence, - Cause-and-effect trap. It implies Hayden's poem caused or produced Ali's poem. The two are independent examples, not a cause and its result.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For transition questions, cover the choices and decide the relationship yourself first: same direction, opposite direction, or cause/effect. Here the second clause echoes the first (another poem about a painting), so the answer must be a same-direction word like "likewise" or "similarly." Spotting parallel examples instantly eliminates every contrast and cause/effect option.

questions.passage: Firefly luciferase (Fluc) is a distinctly evolved enzyme that can oxidize a substrate called D-luciferin to induce bioluminescence and can act as a fatty acyl-CoA synthetase (ACS) enzyme, a class of enzyme present in all insects. __________ Fluc is a bifunctional enzyme whose presence indicates an insect is capable of emitting light; in contrast, the presence of ACS alone would be insufficient for determining bioluminescence.
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is (D) That is,. This is an Expression of Ideas question testing the Transitions skill, rated medium difficulty. The task is to choose the transition that best signals the logical relationship between the first sentence and the second sentence.

Core Concepts
A transition is a word or phrase that signals how one idea relates to another. You must match the transition to the actual logical relationship between the sentences. Key categories tested here:

  • Restatement / clarification ("That is," "In other words,"): the next sentence repeats or simplifies the same idea using different words. It adds no new fact, it relabels what was just said.
  • Contrast / concession ("Nevertheless," "However,"): the next sentence pushes against or qualifies the previous idea.
  • Emphasis / intensification ("In fact,"): the next sentence confirms the prior point and pushes it further, often with a stronger or more surprising detail.
  • Addition ("Moreover," "Furthermore,"): the next sentence introduces a new, additional point on top of the previous one.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Sentence 1: Fluc is described as doing two things, it can oxidize D-luciferin to induce bioluminescence, and it can act as a fatty acyl-CoA synthetase (ACS) enzyme. So we are told Fluc has exactly two functions.
  • Sentence 2: Fluc is called a "bifunctional enzyme" ("bi-" meaning two), and the sentence then explains what that label means for detecting bioluminescence.
  • Relationship: Sentence 2 does not contrast with Sentence 1, and it does not add a third function. It takes the two functions just listed and labels/summarizes them with the single term "bifunctional." That is a restatement or clarification of the same idea.
  • Therefore the blank needs a restatement transition: \(\text{That is,}\) the relabeling word.

Why Each Answer

  • (A) Nevertheless, — Trap: False Contrast. This signals a concession or opposition, but Sentence 2 agrees with and summarizes Sentence 1, so there is no contrast.
  • (B) In fact, — Trap: Wrong Relationship (Intensification). This would signal that Sentence 2 strengthens or adds a surprising confirmation, but Sentence 2 simply renames the two functions already given, it does not escalate the point.
  • (C) Moreover, — Trap: False Addition. This signals a new, additional point, yet Sentence 2 introduces no new information, it consolidates the two functions already stated.
  • (D) That is, — Correct. It signals a restatement/clarification, exactly matching how Sentence 2 condenses Fluc's two listed functions into the single term "bifunctional enzyme."

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When the sentence after the blank re-describes the previous sentence in fewer or simpler words (especially when it introduces a defining label like "bifunctional"), reach for a restatement transition such as "That is," or "In other words," and rule out contrast and addition words. Quick check: if you can mentally replace the transition with "In other words" and the passage still flows, the answer is the restatement choice.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • The South Sudan Workers Trade Union Federation (SSWTUF) is a national union federation for the African nation of South Sudan.
  • It helps improve conditions for workers in that nation.
  • ITUC-Africa is a regional union federation that represents national union federations across Africa.
  • It represents the SSWTUF.
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B. This is an Expression of Ideas question testing the Rhetorical Synthesis skill, and its difficulty is rated easy. Your job is to pick the sentence that best uses the bulleted notes to accomplish one specific rhetorical goal.

Core Concepts
Rhetorical Synthesis questions give you a set of factual notes and a goal stated in the prompt. To answer correctly you must do two things:

  • Read the goal in the prompt literally and identify its exact subject. Here the subject is national union federations and the goal is to explain their purpose (what they do / why they exist).
  • Choose the option that (a) is on that exact subject and (b) delivers that exact goal using the notes. An option can be a true statement and still be wrong if it answers a different goal.

Key facts from the notes: the SSWTUF is a national union federation, it helps improve conditions for workers, ITUC-Africa is a regional federation that represents national federations, and it represents the SSWTUF.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Goal subject = national union federations. Goal action = explain their purpose.
  • Note 1 tells us the SSWTUF is a national union federation. Note 2 tells us its purpose: it helps improve conditions for workers. Combining these two notes states the purpose of a national union federation, using the SSWTUF as a concrete example.
  • Option B does exactly that: it generalizes to "national union federations," gives the SSWTUF as an example, and states the purpose (improving conditions for workers). It matches both the subject and the goal.

Why Each Answer

  • A — Incomplete / Off-Goal: It states a fact about the SSWTUF but never says what national union federations are for. It identifies, it does not explain a purpose.
  • B — Correct: It names the subject (national union federations), uses the SSWTUF as an example, and states the purpose (improving worker conditions), drawing on notes 1 and 2.
  • C — Off-Goal: It describes a relationship (the SSWTUF being represented by ITUC-Africa) instead of a purpose. True, but it answers the wrong question.
  • D — Wrong Subject: It explains the purpose of regional federations like ITUC-Africa, not national federations. The prompt asked about national federations, so the subject is mismatched.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
Underline the exact noun and the exact goal in the prompt before reading the options ("purpose" + "national union federations"). Then eliminate any choice that is about the wrong noun (D) or delivers the wrong goal — a mere fact or a relationship (A and C) — even if it is perfectly true.
questions.question_text: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to explain the purpose of national union federations?

question_options.option_text: National union federations, such as the SSWTUF, work to improve conditions for workers in their member nations.
The SSWTUF is one of the national union federations represented by ITUC-Africa.
The SSWTUF is a national union federation in Africa.
Regional union federations like ITUC-Africa represent the national union federations in a specific area.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Generally, an object will heat up when twisted.
  • The twisting of an object is known as torsion.
  • A 2019 study led by Zunfeng Liu and Ray Baughman tested the torsional heating of various fibers.
  • When a sample of styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene (SEBS) rubber fiber was twisted, its average surface temperature increased by \(3.5^\circ\text{C}\).
  • When a sample of single-ply nickel-titanium (NiTi) wire was twisted, its average surface temperature increased by \(21.3^\circ\text{C}\).
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B. This is an Expression of Ideas question testing the Rhetorical Synthesis skill, rated easy. Your job is to pick the sentence that best uses the notes to accomplish one specific rhetorical goal.

Core Concepts
Rhetorical Synthesis questions give you bullet-point notes and a stated goal. The rules are simple:

  • Read the goal literally and do exactly what it says, nothing more.
  • The goal here is to emphasize a similarity between SEBS rubber and single-ply NiTi wire fibers. A similarity means a trait or result the two share.
  • The winning choice must (1) mention both fibers and (2) state something they have in common, using accurate information from the notes.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • From the notes: twisting (torsion) generally heats an object up. In the 2019 study, the SEBS rubber sample heated up by \(3.5^\circ\text{C}\) and the NiTi wire sample heated up by \(21.3^\circ\text{C}\) when twisted.
  • The shared result is that both fibers heated up when twisted. That is the similarity the goal asks us to emphasize.
  • Scan the options for one that names both fibers and points to this common outcome.
  • Option B does exactly that: it says both SEBS rubber and single-ply NiTi wire fibers heat up when twisted, per the 2019 study.

Why Each Answer

  • A (Incorrect): Out of Scope / Factually Inaccurate. It names both fibers but states no shared characteristic, and it misreads the notes by claiming "two research teams" when the notes describe a single study led by two researchers.
  • B (Correct): It mentions both fibers and states their shared result, that both heat up when twisted, directly emphasizing a similarity.
  • C (Incorrect): Wrong Goal. It highlights a difference (NiTi wire heated more than SEBS rubber), the opposite of emphasizing a similarity.
  • D (Incorrect): Out of Scope. It describes torsional heating in general but never mentions either fiber, so it cannot emphasize a similarity between them.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For "emphasize a similarity" goals, demand two things from the answer: both subjects named AND one shared trait. Cross out any choice that names only one subject (D) or that contrasts them (C). The word "Both" in option B is a strong signal it is doing the comparison work the goal requires.
questions.question_text: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between SEBS rubber and single-ply NiTi wire fibers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

question_options.option_text: Twisting an object will generally cause its temperature to increase, a process known as torsional heating.
Researchers determined that when the fibers were twisted, the average surface temperature of single-ply NiTi wire increased more than that of SEBS rubber.
In 2019, two research teams observed the effects of torsional heating on various fibers, including SEBS rubber and single-ply NiTi wire.
Both SEBS rubber and single-ply NiTi wire fibers heat up when twisted, according to a 2019 study.

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
This is a Student-Produced Response (SPR) question from the Advanced Math domain, skill: Nonlinear functions, rated hard. A possible value of \(x\) is \(2.4\) (the other accepted value is \(4.8\)). You enter either one.

Core Concepts

  • A quadratic function graphs as a parabola. When it opens downward, its highest point is the vertex, which here represents the maximum height.
  • Vertex form: \(h(t) = a(t - k)^2 + p\), where \((k, p)\) is the vertex. The leading coefficient \(a\) controls the width and direction; \(a < 0\) means the parabola opens downward (a peak).
  • Symmetry: a parabola is symmetric about the vertical line through its vertex (\(t = k\)). So any height below the maximum is reached at two times, equally spaced before and after the peak.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

Identify the known points from the problem:

  • Launched from the ground: \(h(0) = 0\) feet at \(t = 0\) seconds.
  • Maximum height: vertex at \(t = 3.6\) seconds, \(h = 207.36\) feet.

Write the model in vertex form using the vertex \((3.6,\ 207.36)\):

\[h(t) = a(t - 3.6)^2 + 207.36\]

Use the launch point \(h(0) = 0\) to find \(a\):

\[0 = a(0 - 3.6)^2 + 207.36\]

\[0 = a(12.96) + 207.36\]

\[a(12.96) = -207.36\]

\[a = \frac{-207.36}{12.96} = -16\]

So the height model is:

\[h(t) = -16(t - 3.6)^2 + 207.36\]

Now set the height equal to \(184.32\) feet and solve for the time \(x\):

\[184.32 = -16(x - 3.6)^2 + 207.36\]

\[-16(x - 3.6)^2 = 184.32 - 207.36 = -23.04\]

\[(x - 3.6)^2 = \frac{-23.04}{-16} = 1.44\]

Take the square root of both sides (remember the \(\pm\)):

\[x - 3.6 = \pm 1.2\]

\[x = 3.6 + 1.2 = 4.8 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 3.6 - 1.2 = 2.4\]

Both times are physically valid: \(2.4\) seconds is on the way up, and \(4.8\) seconds is on the way down. Either is an acceptable answer.

Why Each Answer

  • \(2.4\) (correct): the object passes \(184.32\) feet while still rising, \(1.2\) seconds before reaching the peak. Plugging back in: \(-16(2.4 - 3.6)^2 + 207.36 = -16(1.44) + 207.36 = -23.04 + 207.36 = 184.32\). ✓
  • \(4.8\) (also correct): the object passes the same height while falling, \(1.2\) seconds after the peak, by symmetry. \(-16(4.8 - 3.6)^2 + 207.36 = 184.32\). ✓
  • Common trap — \(3.6\): that is the time of the maximum height (\(207.36\) feet), not the target height. Picking it confuses the vertex time with the requested height.
  • Common trap — forgetting the \(\pm\): only taking the positive root gives \(4.8\) and misses \(2.4\); only the negative gives \(2.4\) and misses \(4.8\). Either single value is accepted, but knowing both confirms the work.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When you know the vertex and one other point, vertex form is fastest: drop in \((k, p)\), then use the extra point to find \(a\). For height problems, the leading coefficient often comes out to \(-16\) (feet) because of gravity. In Desmos you could graph \(y = -16(x-3.6)^2 + 207.36\) and \(y = 184.32\) and read off the two intersection x-values, \(2.4\) and \(4.8\).
questions.question_text: A quadratic function models the height, in feet, of an object above the ground in terms of the time, in seconds, after the object was launched. The model estimates that the object was launched from an initial height of \(0.00\) feet above the ground and was at a maximum height of \(207.36\) feet above the ground \(3.6\) seconds after it was launched. The model also estimates that the object was at a height of \(184.32\) feet above the ground \(x\) seconds after it was launched. What is a possible value of \(x\)?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is \(400\) (choice A). This is an Algebra question testing Linear functions, and it is rated easy. The task is to evaluate a function at a specific input value.

Core Concepts

  • Function notation: \(h(x)\) is a rule that takes an input \(x\) and produces an output. The expression after the equals sign tells you exactly what to do to the input.
  • Evaluating a function: To find \(h(10)\), you replace every \(x\) in the rule with the number \(10\), then simplify using the order of operations (parentheses first, then multiplication).
  • Order of operations: Work inside the parentheses before multiplying by the number outside.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Start with the rule: \(h(x) = 5(9x - 10)\).
  • Substitute \(x = 10\): \[h(10) = 5\big(9(10) - 10\big)\]
  • Multiply inside the parentheses: \(9 \times 10 = 90\), giving \[h(10) = 5(90 - 10)\]
  • Subtract inside the parentheses: \(90 - 10 = 80\), giving \[h(10) = 5(80)\]
  • Multiply: \(5 \times 80 = 400\), so \[h(10) = 400\]

Why Each Answer

  • A. \(400\) — Correct. It is the result of correctly substituting and simplifying \(5(9(10) - 10)\).
  • B. \(10\) — Incorrect (Restates the Input). This is just the input value \(x = 10\), not the output. It ignores the function rule entirely.
  • C. \(50\) — Incorrect (Partial Computation). This comes from computing only \(5 \times 10 = 50\), dropping the \(9x\) term and the structure of the expression.
  • D. \(90\) — Incorrect (Stops Too Early). This is the value of \(9x = 9(10) = 90\) alone, before subtracting \(10\) and multiplying by \(5\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When you see \(h(10)\), read it as "plug \(10\) in for \(x\)." Substitute first, then simplify strictly inside-out: parentheses before the outer multiplication. You can verify instantly in Desmos by typing \(h(x)=5(9x-10)\) and then \(h(10)\).
questions.question_text: The function \(h\) is defined by \(h(x) = 5(9x - 10)\). What is the value of \(h(10)\)?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is D, \(c + d \leq 43\). This is an Algebra question testing linear inequalities in one or two variables. Difficulty: easy.

Core Concepts

  • Combining two groups: When a total is made up of two separate counts, you ADD them. Here the total animals \(=\) cats \(+\) dogs \(= c + d\).
  • Inequality vocabulary: The phrase at most means "no more than," i.e. the value can equal the limit or be less, but never exceed it. In symbols this is less than or equal to, written \(\leq\).
  • Compare: "at least" means \(\geq\) (the value can be that number or larger).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Step 1: Write the total number of animals. Cats plus dogs gives \(c + d\).
  • Step 2: Translate the limit. "Can care for at most \(43\) animals" means the total is allowed to be \(43\) or fewer, so \(c + d\) is less than or equal to \(43\).
  • Step 3: Put it together: \(c + d \leq 43\).

Why Each Answer

  • A) \(c - d \leq 43\): Incorrect. Uses subtraction, but a total comes from adding the two groups, not finding their difference.
  • B) \(c - d \geq 43\): Incorrect. Wrong operation (subtraction) AND wrong direction (\(\geq\) means "at least," the opposite of "at most").
  • C) \(c + d \geq 43\): Incorrect. The sum is right, but \(\geq\) reverses the meaning. "At most" caps the total, so it cannot be "\(\geq 43\)" (which would allow huge numbers).
  • D) \(c + d \leq 43\): Correct. Adds the two groups and uses \(\leq\) to cap the total at \(43\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
Lock in two triggers: "at most" \(\to \leq\) and "at least" \(\to \geq\). Then decide add vs. subtract by asking "is this a combined total?" If yes, add. Eliminating the two subtraction choices instantly leaves only the direction decision.
questions.question_text: A pet service that takes care of both cats and dogs can care for at most \(43\) animals. Which inequality represents this situation, where \(c\) is the number of cats and \(d\) is the number of dogs?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is \(k = 17\). This is an Algebra question testing Linear equations in one variable, at an easy difficulty level. You must find the value of the constant \(k\) that makes the equation \(9x + 17 = 9x + k\) true for every possible value of \(x\).

Core Concepts

  • Linear equation in one variable: an equation that can be written so the variable (here \(x\)) appears only to the first power.
  • Number of solutions: A linear equation can have exactly one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
    • One solution: the variable terms differ, so you can solve for a single value of \(x\).
    • No solution: the variable terms are identical but the constant terms differ (you get a false statement like \(17 = 5\)).
    • Infinitely many solutions: the two sides are exactly identical, so the equation is true no matter what \(x\) is. This requires the coefficient of \(x\) to match on both sides AND the constant terms to match on both sides.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Start with the equation: \(9x + 17 = 9x + k\).
  • Subtract \(9x\) from both sides to remove the variable terms: \(9x + 17 - 9x = 9x + k - 9x\), which simplifies to \(17 = k\).
  • The variable has been eliminated entirely. For the original equation to be true for all \(x\) (infinitely many solutions), what remains, \(17 = k\), must be a true statement.
  • Therefore \(k = 17\).

Why Each Answer

  • Correct value, \(k = 17\): When \(k = 17\), the equation becomes \(9x + 17 = 9x + 17\), where the left and right sides are identical. Every value of \(x\) satisfies it, giving infinitely many solutions.
  • Any value where \(k \ne 17\) (trap — No Solution): If \(k\) were anything other than 17, subtracting \(9x\) would leave a false statement such as \(17 = k\) being untrue (for example \(17 = 5\)). That produces no solution, not infinitely many.
  • Answering 0 (trap — Misreading the condition): A common mistake is to set the constant to 0 or to move 17 to the other side. But the constants must be equal to each other, not zero, so \(k\) must equal 17.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For "infinitely many solutions" problems, the two sides of the equation must be carbon copies of each other. A fast trigger: cancel the matching variable terms, and whatever constant remains on the other side is your answer. Here, canceling \(9x\) immediately leaves \(k = 17\).
questions.question_text:
\(9x + 17 = 9x + k\)
In the given equation, \(k\) is a constant. The equation has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of \(k\)?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is \(6\). This is an Advanced Math question on Nonlinear functions (exponential functions), rated easy. You are asked for the \(y\)-coordinate of the \(y\)-intercept of the exponential graph \(y = 6(1.85)^x\).

Core Concepts

  • The \(y\)-intercept of any graph is the point where the curve crosses the \(y\)-axis. On the \(y\)-axis the \(x\)-coordinate is always \(0\), so the \(y\)-intercept has the form \((0, y)\). To find it, substitute \(x = 0\).
  • An exponential function has the form \(y = a\,b^{x}\), where \(a\) is the starting value (the \(y\)-intercept) and \(b\) is the growth factor. Here \(a = 6\) and \(b = 1.85\).
  • Zero-exponent rule: any nonzero number raised to the power \(0\) equals \(1\). In symbols, \(b^{0} = 1\) for any \(b \neq 0\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Step 1: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \[y = 6(1.85)^{0}.\]
  • Step 2: Apply the zero-exponent rule to the base \(1.85\): \[(1.85)^{0} = 1.\]
  • Step 3: Multiply: \[y = 6 \times 1 = 6.\]
  • So the \(y\)-intercept is \((0, 6)\), and the value of \(y\) is \(6\).

Why This Answer
Because \(x = 0\) on the \(y\)-axis and \((1.85)^{0} = 1\), the entire factor with the exponent collapses to \(1\), leaving just the coefficient \(6\). Notice this matches the shortcut below: the coefficient in front of an exponential is always the \(y\)-intercept. A common trap is multiplying \(6 \times 1.85 = 11.1\) by forgetting the zero exponent, or answering \(1.85\) by reading off the base instead of evaluating the function.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For any exponential written as \(y = a\,b^{x}\), the \(y\)-intercept is simply \(a\) (the number multiplied out front), because \(b^{0} = 1\). You can read it off directly without computing. You can also confirm by graphing \(y = 6(1.85)^x\) in Desmos and checking where it crosses the \(y\)-axis.
questions.question_text: The \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = 6(1.85)^x\) in the \(xy\)-plane is \((0, y)\). What is the value of \(y\)?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot The correct answer is A, \(\frac{1}{6}\). This is an Algebra item testing Linear functions (medium difficulty): read two points off a graphed line and compute its slope.

Core Concepts The slope of a line measures its steepness as the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change between any two points on the line. For points \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\), the slope is \[m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}.\] A positive slope means the line rises from left to right; a negative slope means it falls. The y-intercept is the y-value where the line crosses the y-axis, a separate quantity from the slope.

Step-by-Step Breakdown Read two points where the line passes exactly through grid intersections: \((-6, -8)\) and \((6, -6)\). Substitute into the slope formula: \[m = \frac{-6 - (-8)}{6 - (-6)} = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}.\] The line rises gently from left to right, consistent with a small positive slope.

Why Each Answer Choice A, \(\frac{1}{6}\), matches the computed slope and is correct. Choice B, \(-7\), is the approximate y-intercept of the line, not its slope (confusing intercept with slope). Choice C, \(-\frac{1}{6}\), has the right magnitude but the wrong sign; the line rises, so the slope is positive, not negative. Choice D, \(7\), takes the y-intercept's magnitude and treats it as the slope (intercept/slope confusion plus sign error).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway A line that climbs only one unit over a span of many units must have a small positive slope. Before computing, estimate: a nearly flat, rising line has a slope between 0 and 1, which immediately rules out \(-7\), \(-\frac{1}{6}\), and \(7\).
questions.question_text: The graph of the linear function \(f\) is shown, where \(y = f(x)\). What is the slope of the graph of \(f\)?

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is \(31{,}152\) yards per hour. This is a Problem-Solving and Data Analysis question testing the skill of ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units (unit conversion). Difficulty: medium.

Core Concepts

  • A rate compares two quantities with different units, such as miles per hour (distance per time).
  • Unit conversion means rewriting a measurement in a different unit without changing its actual size. You multiply by a conversion factor, which is a fraction equal to \(1\).
  • The given relationship is \(1 \text{ mile} = 1{,}760 \text{ yards}\). This lets us build the conversion factor \(\frac{1{,}760 \text{ yards}}{1 \text{ mile}}\), which equals \(1\) because the top and bottom describe the same length.
  • When you multiply, the "miles" unit cancels and you are left with "yards."

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Start with the given speed: \(17.700\) miles per hour, written as \(\frac{17.700 \text{ miles}}{1 \text{ hour}}\).
  • Multiply by the conversion factor so that miles cancel: \[\frac{17.700 \text{ miles}}{1 \text{ hour}} \times \frac{1{,}760 \text{ yards}}{1 \text{ mile}}.\]
  • The "miles" units cancel, leaving yards per hour. Now multiply the numbers: \[17.700 \times 1{,}760 = 31{,}152.\]
  • So the average speed is \(31{,}152\) yards per hour.

Why This Answer
Because there are \(1{,}760\) yards in every mile, each mile per hour equals \(1{,}760\) yards per hour. Scaling the given \(17.700\) miles per hour by this factor gives \(31{,}152\) yards per hour. A common trap is to divide instead of multiply (since yards are smaller than miles, the number must get larger, so multiplication is correct). Another trap is misplacing the decimal in \(17.700 \times 1{,}760\); careful column multiplication confirms \(31{,}152\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
Set up conversions as fractions and let units cancel like algebra symbols. If the new unit is smaller than the old one, expect a bigger number, which is a quick sanity check on whether to multiply or divide.
questions.question_text:
A triathlon is a multisport race consisting of three different legs. A triathlon participant completed the cycling leg with an average speed of \(17.700\) miles per hour. What was the average speed, in yards per hour, of the participant during the cycling leg?
(\(1 \text{ mile} = 1,760 \text{ yards}\))

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is A, \(\sin D = \frac{612}{613}\). This is a Geometry and Trigonometry question testing Right triangles and trigonometry, at a medium difficulty level.

Core Concepts

  • Similar triangles: Two triangles are similar when they have the same shape. Their corresponding angles are equal, so if angle \(A\) corresponds to angle \(D\), then \(A\) and \(D\) have the exact same measure.
  • Trig ratios in a right triangle (with the right angle as the reference for naming sides): for an acute angle, \(\tan = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\) and \(\sin = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\). The hypotenuse is the side across from the right angle.
  • Pythagorean theorem: in a right triangle with legs \(a\) and \(b\) and hypotenuse \(c\), \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Because the triangles are similar with \(A\) corresponding to \(D\), the angles are equal: \(\angle A = \angle D\). Equal angles have equal trig values, so \(\sin D = \sin A\). Finding \(\sin A\) solves the problem.
  • Angle \(C\) is the right angle, so the side opposite \(A\) and the side adjacent to \(A\) are the two legs. From \(\tan A = \frac{612}{35}\), let the opposite leg be \(612\) and the adjacent leg be \(35\).
  • Find the hypotenuse with the Pythagorean theorem: \[\text{hyp}^2 = 612^2 + 35^2 = 374544 + 1225 = 375769.\] Taking the square root gives \(\text{hyp} = \sqrt{375769} = 613\).
  • Now compute the sine: \[\sin A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{612}{613}.\] Therefore \(\sin D = \frac{612}{613}\).

Why Each Answer

  • A) \(\frac{612}{613}\) — Correct. This is \(\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\) for angle \(A\) (and thus \(D\)).
  • B) \(\frac{35}{613}\) — Incorrect (Wrong ratio). This is \(\cos A\), the adjacent leg over the hypotenuse, not the sine.
  • C) \(\frac{613}{612}\) — Incorrect (Inverted ratio). This flips sine upside down; sine is never the hypotenuse over a leg.
  • D) \(\frac{613}{35}\) — Incorrect (Inverted/wrong ratio). This is the reciprocal of cosine (hypotenuse over adjacent) and does not represent any sine value here.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When two triangles are similar, equal corresponding angles share identical trig ratios, so you can ignore which triangle is named and just work the angle you know. Recognize \((35, 612, 613)\) as a Pythagorean triple to skip the square-root arithmetic, and remember SOH-CAH-TOA: sine always uses the hypotenuse on the bottom.
questions.question_text: Triangle \(ABC\) is similar to triangle \(DEF\), where angle \(A\) corresponds to angle \(D\) and angle \(C\) corresponds to angle \(F\). Angles \(C\) and \(F\) are right angles. If \(\tan A = \frac{612}{35}\), what is the value of \(\sin D\)?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is C. This is an Advanced Math question testing the skill of interpreting Nonlinear functions in context. Difficulty: medium. The goal is to translate the function statement \(A(18) = 2{,}268\) into a plain-English description of the triangle.

Core Concepts

  • A function written as \(A(b)\) takes an input (the value inside the parentheses, here \(b\)) and produces an output (the value the function equals).
  • Here the input \(b\) is the length of the triangle's base in centimeters, and the output \(A(b)\) is the area in square centimeters \((\text{cm}^2)\).
  • So \(A(18) = 2{,}268\) is read as: "when the input (base) is \(18\), the output (area) is \(2{,}268\)."
  • Area of a triangle: \(\text{Area} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,(\text{base})(\text{height})\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • The base length is \(b\) cm and the height is \(14\) times the base, so the height is \(14b\) cm.
  • Substitute into the area formula: \(\text{Area} = \tfrac{1}{2}(b)(14b) = 7b^2\). This matches the given function \(A(b) = 7b^2\), confirming \(A\) outputs the area.
  • Identify the input and output in \(A(18) = 2{,}268\): the input is \(b = 18\) (the base, in cm) and the output is \(2{,}268\) (the area, in \(\text{cm}^2\)).
  • Check: \(A(18) = 7(18)^2 = 7(324) = 2{,}268\). Correct.
  • In words: if the base is \(18\text{ cm}\), then the area is \(2{,}268\text{ cm}^2\).

Why Each Answer

  • C (correct): States the base is \(18\text{ cm}\) and the area is \(2{,}268\text{ cm}^2\) — exactly the input-to-output meaning of \(A(18)=2{,}268\).
  • A (incorrect — Swaps input/output and wrong quantity): Calls \(2{,}268\) the base and \(18\) the height. It reverses the roles and treats the output as a length rather than an area.
  • B (incorrect — Confuses area with height): Correctly uses \(18\) as the base but labels the output \(2{,}268\) as the height. The output of \(A\) is the area, not the height.
  • D (incorrect — Swaps input/output): Reverses the values, making \(2{,}268\) the base and \(18\) the area. The input \(18\) is the base and the output \(2{,}268\) is the area, not the reverse.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For "interpret \(f(\text{input}) = \text{output}\)" questions, always pin down two things first: what the number inside the parentheses measures (here, the base) and what the function's value measures (here, the area). The answer is simply "when input is __, output is __" — and watch for traps that swap the two or rename the output.
questions.question_text: The function \(A(b) = 7b^2\) gives the area of a right triangle, in square centimeters (\(\text{cm}^2\)), if the length of its base is \(b \text{ cm}\) and the length of its height is \(14\) times the length of its base. Which of the following is the best interpretation of \(A(18) = 2,268\)?

question_options.option_text: If the length of the base of the triangle is \(2,268 \text{ cm}\), then the area of the triangle is \(18 \text{ cm}^2\).
If the length of the base of the triangle is \(18 \text{ cm}\), then the length of the height of the triangle is \(2,268 \text{ cm}\).
If the length of the base of the triangle is \(2,268 \text{ cm}\), then the length of the height of the triangle is \(18 \text{ cm}\).
If the length of the base of the triangle is \(18 \text{ cm}\), then the area of the triangle is \(2,268 \text{ cm}^2\).

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is C) \(9\). This is an Advanced Math question on the skill of solving nonlinear equations in one variable. Difficulty: easy.

Core Concepts

  • Zero Product Property: If a product of factors equals zero, then at least one of the factors must equal zero. In symbols, if \(a \cdot b \cdot c = 0\), then \(a = 0\) or \(b = 0\) or \(c = 0\).
  • Constant factors: A nonzero constant multiplier (like \(-4\)) can never be zero, so it does not produce any solution. Only the factors that contain the variable matter.
  • Solution of an equation: A value of the variable that makes the equation true. Here, any value of \(v\) that makes one factor equal to zero is a solution.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Start with \(-4(v - 9)(v - 2)(v + 7) = 0\).
  • The factor \(-4\) is a nonzero constant, so it can be ignored when finding solutions.
  • Set each variable factor equal to zero:
    \(v - 9 = 0 \Rightarrow v = 9\)
    \(v - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow v = 2\)
    \(v + 7 = 0 \Rightarrow v = -7\)
  • The complete solution set is \(v = 9,\ 2,\ -7\).
  • Compare these solutions to the answer choices. Only \(9\) appears as an option.

Why Each Answer

  • A) \(-2\): Incorrect. This is a sign-flip trap. The factor is \((v - 2)\), which gives \(v = 2\), not \(-2\).
  • B) \(7\): Incorrect. This is a sign-confusion trap. The factor is \((v + 7)\), which gives \(v = -7\), not \(+7\).
  • C) \(9\): Correct. The factor \((v - 9)\) equals zero when \(v = 9\), making the entire product zero.
  • D) \(-4\): Incorrect. This is a distractor pulled from the leading constant \(-4\). A constant coefficient is never a solution of the equation.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For a factored equation set equal to zero, read each solution by flipping the sign of the number inside each variable factor: \((v - 9)\) gives \(+9\), and \((v + 7)\) gives \(-7\). Ignore any constant out front. To verify quickly, you can graph the expression in Desmos and read the \(x\)-intercepts.
questions.question_text:
\(-4(v - 9)(v - 2)(v + 7) = 0\)
What value of \(v\) is a solution to the given equation?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is D) \(208\pi\). This is a Geometry and Trigonometry question testing the skill of Area and volume, at a medium difficulty level. You are given one circle's radius and another circle's area, and asked for their combined area.

Core Concepts

  • The area of a circle is found with the formula \(A = \pi r^2\), where \(r\) is the radius (the distance from the center to the edge).
  • The notation \(r^2\) means \(r \times r\).
  • The symbol \(\pi\) (pi) is a constant; here we keep answers in terms of \(\pi\) rather than converting to a decimal.
  • "Total area" of two separate circles simply means you add their two individual areas together.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Find the area of circle \(K\). Its radius is \(8\) mm, so substitute \(r = 8\) into \(A = \pi r^2\): \[A_K = \pi (8)^2 = \pi \times 64 = 64\pi \text{ mm}^2\]
  • Identify the area of circle \(L\). The problem gives it directly: \(A_L = 144\pi \text{ mm}^2\). No calculation is needed for this one.
  • Add the two areas. Combine the like terms (both have \(\pi\)): \[A_K + A_L = 64\pi + 144\pi = 208\pi \text{ mm}^2\]

Why Each Answer

  • A) \(40\pi\): Incorrect. This treats the given numbers carelessly (for example doubling the radius to get a diameter of \(16\) and adding pieces incorrectly). It ignores that circle \(K\)'s area must come from squaring the radius.
  • B) \(20\pi\): Incorrect. This appears to use \(2 \times 8 + 4 = 20\) or similar arithmetic that never applies the area formula \(A = \pi r^2\). Trap type: misused formula.
  • C) \(80\pi\): Incorrect. This likely results from computing circle \(K\)'s area as \(64\pi\) but then mis-adding, or from confusing the radius with a side length. Trap type: arithmetic slip.
  • D) \(208\pi\): Correct. \(64\pi + 144\pi = 208\pi\), the true sum of the two areas.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When a problem mixes "radius given" with "area given," convert everything to the same quantity first (here, area) before combining. Keeping \(\pi\) symbolic lets you add coefficients directly: \(64\pi + 144\pi = (64 + 144)\pi\). Mental trigger: square the radius, then just add the \(\pi\) terms.
questions.question_text: Circle \(K\) has a radius of \(8\) millimeters (mm). Circle \(L\) has an area of \(144\pi \text{ mm}^2\). What is the total area, in \(\text{mm}^2\), of circles \(K\) and \(L\)?

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is A: \(\dfrac{-49 + \sqrt{(49)^2 - 4(1)(1)}}{2(1)}\). This is an Advanced Math question on the skill of nonlinear (quadratic) equations in one variable. Difficulty: medium.

Core Concepts

  • A quadratic equation is any equation that can be written as \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants and \(a \neq 0\).
  • The quadratic formula gives the solutions of \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\): \[x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}.\] Here \(a\) is the coefficient of \(x^2\), \(b\) is the coefficient of \(x\), and \(c\) is the constant term.
  • The \(\pm\) symbol means there are generally two solutions: one using \(+\) and one using \(-\). The question asks for just one of them.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Compare \(x^2 + 49x + 1 = 0\) to the standard form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\).
  • The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(1\), so \(a = 1\).
  • The coefficient of \(x\) is \(49\), so \(b = 49\).
  • The constant term is \(1\), so \(c = 1\).
  • Substitute into the quadratic formula: \[x = \frac{-49 \pm \sqrt{(49)^2 - 4(1)(1)}}{2(1)}.\]
  • Taking the \(+\) sign gives one valid solution: \(\dfrac{-49 + \sqrt{(49)^2 - 4(1)(1)}}{2(1)}\), which is exactly choice A.

Why Each Answer

  • A (correct): Substitutes \(a=1\), \(b=49\), \(c=1\) correctly into the quadratic formula, giving a genuine solution of the equation.
  • B (incorrect): Uses \(a=49\) in the \(b^2 - 4ac\) term and in the denominator \(2a\). This confuses the coefficients (treats \(49\) as the leading coefficient). The equation's \(a\) is \(1\), not \(49\).
  • C (incorrect): Swaps \(b\) and \(c\), using \(b=1\) and \(c=49\). This solves the wrong equation \(x^2 + x + 49 = 0\), not the given one.
  • D (incorrect): Mixes up the coefficients further, using \(-1\) for \(-b\) while putting \(2(49)\) in the denominator. The substitution is inconsistent with the actual values \(a=1\), \(b=49\), \(c=1\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When a question asks you to identify the quadratic-formula expression rather than a decimal value, do not simplify. Just read off \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) directly from the equation in standard form and match them to \(\dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\). The denominator should be \(2a = 2(1)\) and the leading number after the minus should be \(-b = -49\) — a quick check that instantly rules out B, C, and D.
questions.question_text:
\(x^2 + 49x + 1 = 0\)
What is one of the solutions to the given equation?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is D: \(I = 800(0.5)^{\frac{x}{7}}\). This is an Advanced Math question testing Nonlinear functions, specifically writing an exponential decay model. Difficulty: medium.

Core Concepts

  • Exponential model: When a quantity changes by a fixed percentage over equal intervals, it is modeled by \(I = a\,(b)^{\frac{x}{k}}\).
  • \(a\) is the initial value (the amount when \(x = 0\)).
  • \(b\) is the growth/decay factor per interval: \(b > 1\) means growth, \(0 < b < 1\) means decay.
  • \(k\) is the interval length — the amount of \(x\) needed for one full multiplication by \(b\). Dividing the exponent by \(k\) makes the factor apply once per \(k\) units.
  • Percentage to factor: a decrease of \(p\%\) leaves \(100\% - p\%\) of the amount, so the factor is \(b = 1 - \frac{p}{100}\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Step 1 — initial value: The beam starts with \(800\) photons at the surface, so \(a = 800\).
  • Step 2 — decay factor: The number of photons decreases by \(50\%\) over each interval. Remaining \(= 100\% - 50\% = 50\% = 0.5\), so \(b = 0.5\).
  • Step 3 — interval length: The \(50\%\) drop happens for every \(7\) millimeters, so \(k = 7\). Because \(x\) is measured in millimeters, the exponent must be \(\frac{x}{7}\) so that one full halving occurs each \(7\) mm.
  • Step 4 — assemble: Substituting gives \(I = 800(0.5)^{\frac{x}{7}}\).
  • Check: At \(x = 0\), \(I = 800(0.5)^0 = 800\) (correct start). At \(x = 7\), \(I = 800(0.5)^1 = 400\) (halved after 7 mm, correct).

Why Each Answer

  • A) \(I = 800(7)^{\frac{x}{2}}\): Wrong. The base \(7\) and interval \(2\) swap the roles of the rate and the distance, and base \(7 > 1\) describes rapid growth, not a decrease. (Confuses interval with base / growth vs. decay.)
  • B) \(I = 800(0.5)^x\): Wrong. This halves the beam every single millimeter instead of every \(7\) mm; it omits the \(\frac{1}{7}\) interval scaling. (Missing interval length.)
  • C) \(I = 800(2)^{\frac{x}{7}}\): Wrong. Base \(2\) means the count doubles every \(7\) mm — growth, not the \(50\%\) decrease described. (Growth vs. decay confusion.)
  • D) \(I = 800(0.5)^{\frac{x}{7}}\): Correct. Initial \(800\), factor \(0.5\) for the \(50\%\) loss, and exponent \(\frac{x}{7}\) for the \(7\)-mm interval.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For "changes by \(p\%\) every \(k\) units" problems, plug the template \(a(b)^{\frac{x}{k}}\) directly: \(a\) = start, \(b = 1 \pm \frac{p}{100}\) (minus for a decrease), \(k\) = the interval. A decrease always gives a base strictly between \(0\) and \(1\), so you can eliminate any option whose base is \(\ge 1\) immediately.
questions.question_text: A model estimates that the initial number of photons in an X-ray beam is \(800\) when the beam reaches the surface of a certain material. The model also estimates that when the beam passes through this material, the number of photons in the beam decreases by \(50\%\) for each \(7 \text{ millimeters}\) of the material the beam passes through. Which equation represents this model, where \(I\) is the estimated number of photons in the beam when the beam reaches a point \(x \text{ millimeters}\) from the surface?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B, \(5x + 3y = 15\). This is an Algebra question testing the skill of writing linear equations in two variables. Difficulty: medium.

Core Concepts

  • Slope: For any two points \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\), the slope is \(m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), the change in \(y\) divided by the change in \(x\).
  • Slope-intercept form: \(y = mx + b\), where \(m\) is the slope and \(b\) is the \(y\)-intercept (the \(y\)-value where the line crosses the \(y\)-axis, i.e. where \(x = 0\)).
  • Standard form: \(Ax + By = C\). All four answer choices are written in this form, so we will convert our equation to match.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • The two given points are \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 5)\).
  • Find the slope: \(m = \dfrac{5 - 0}{0 - 3} = -\dfrac{5}{3}\).
  • The point \((0, 5)\) has \(x = 0\), so it is the \(y\)-intercept: \(b = 5\).
  • Write slope-intercept form: \(y = -\dfrac{5}{3}x + 5\).
  • Clear the fraction by multiplying every term by \(3\): \(3y = -5x + 15\).
  • Add \(5x\) to both sides to reach standard form: \(5x + 3y = 15\).

To confirm, test both points in \(5x + 3y = 15\): for \((3, 0)\), \(5(3) + 3(0) = 15\) ✓; for \((0, 5)\), \(5(0) + 3(5) = 15\) ✓.

Why Each Answer

  • A) \(3x - 5y = 15\): Incorrect. Testing \((0, 5)\) gives \(3(0) - 5(5) = -25 eq 15\). This swaps and mis-signs the coefficients (Confuses slope numerator/denominator and sign).
  • B) \(5x + 3y = 15\): Correct. Both given points satisfy it, as shown above.
  • C) \(3x + 5y = 15\): Incorrect. Testing \((0, 5)\) gives \(3(0) + 5(5) = 25 eq 15\). The coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\) are swapped (Confuses which intercept pairs with which variable).
  • D) \(5x - 3y = 15\): Incorrect. Testing \((0, 5)\) gives \(5(0) - 3(5) = -15 eq 15\). Uses the wrong sign on the \(y\)-term (Sign error on slope).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When a question gives you the two intercepts \((a, 0)\) and \((0, b)\), use intercept form \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1\) directly: here \(\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{5} = 1\), and multiplying by \(15\) instantly gives \(5x + 3y = 15\). Even faster on test day: plug both given points into the choices and keep the only equation that both points satisfy.
questions.question_text: In the \(xy\)-plane, line \(k\) passes through the points \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 5)\). Which of the following is an equation of line \(k\)?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot The correct answer is D) \(34^\circ\). This is a Geometry and Trigonometry item (skill: Lines, angles, and triangles), rated easy. It asks for the measure of \(\angle C\) in right triangle \(ABC\).

Core Concepts A right triangle contains one \(90^\circ\) angle (here at vertex \(B\), shown by the small square). The three interior angles of any triangle sum to \(180^\circ\). Removing the right angle leaves the two acute angles, which must therefore add to \(180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\); they are complementary.

Step-by-Step Breakdown From the figure, \(\angle B = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle A = 56^\circ\). Using the complementary relationship of the two acute angles: \[\angle C = 90^\circ - \angle A = 90^\circ - 56^\circ = 34^\circ.\] As a check, the full angle sum gives \(180^\circ - 90^\circ - 56^\circ = 34^\circ\), the same result.

Why Each Answer D) \(34^\circ\) is correct because it is the complement of the \(56^\circ\) angle. A) \(124^\circ\) is the trap of computing \(180^\circ - 56^\circ\) (treating the angles as supplementary and ignoring the right angle). B) \(146^\circ\) comes from \(90^\circ + 56^\circ\), adding instead of subtracting. C) \(56^\circ\) simply repeats the given angle \(A\), assuming the two acute angles are equal, which would only hold for an isosceles right triangle.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway In any right triangle the two non-right angles are complementary, so just subtract the known acute angle from \(90^\circ\). Spotting the right-angle square instantly turns the problem into \(90 - \text{given}\).
questions.question_text: In right triangle \(ABC\) shown, what is the measure of \(\angle C\)?

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is \(25\). This is an Algebra question testing systems of two linear equations in two variables, at a medium difficulty level. Rather than asking for \(x\) or \(y\) alone, it asks for the value of the combined expression \(3x - 5y\).

Core Concepts

  • A system of linear equations is two equations that share the same variables \(x\) and \(y\). The solution \((x, y)\) is the single pair of values that makes BOTH equations true at the same time.
  • Elimination means adding or subtracting whole equations to cancel a variable. You may add equations side by side, subtract one from another, or multiply an entire equation by a constant first.
  • Key shortcut: when a question asks for a combination like \(3x - 5y\), you often do NOT need to find \(x\) and \(y\) separately. If adding or subtracting the given equations directly produces that exact expression, you can read off the answer in one step.

Step-by-Step Breakdown
The two equations are:

\[x + 4y = -3\]

\[4x - y = 22\]

Notice that subtracting the first equation from the second targets the expression we want. Subtract term by term, remembering that subtracting a negative becomes addition on the right side:

\[(4x - y) - (x + 4y) = 22 - (-3)\]

Distribute the minus sign across the parentheses on the left:

\[4x - y - x - 4y = 22 + 3\]

Combine like terms: \(4x - x = 3x\) and \(-y - 4y = -5y\), while \(22 + 3 = 25\):

\[3x - 5y = 25\]

The expression we were asked for appears directly, so \(3x - 5y = 25\).

Confirmation by full solve: Multiply the first equation by \(4\) to get \(4x + 16y = -12\), then subtract the second equation: \((4x + 16y) - (4x - y) = -12 - 22\), giving \(17y = -34\), so \(y = -2\). Substitute into the first equation: \(x + 4(-2) = -3 \Rightarrow x - 8 = -3 \Rightarrow x = 5\). Then \(3x - 5y = 3(5) - 5(-2) = 15 + 10 = 25\). The two methods agree.

Why Each Answer
This is a student-produced response question, so there are no multiple-choice traps. The single correct value is \(25\). A common error is to stop after finding only \(x = 5\) or only \(y = -2\) and enter that as the answer; the question specifically asks for the combined expression \(3x - 5y\), not an individual variable. Another error is mishandling the double negative \(22 - (-3)\) and writing \(19\) instead of \(25\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When a system question asks for a linear combination of \(x\) and \(y\), first check whether simply adding or subtracting the two equations builds that exact combination. Here, subtracting equation 1 from equation 2 instantly produced \(3x - 5y\), saving all the work of solving for each variable. You can also verify with Desmos by graphing both lines, reading the intersection point \((5, -2)\), and evaluating the expression.
questions.question_text:
\(x + 4y = -3\)
\(4x - y = 22\)
The solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of \(3x - 5y\)?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B: \((x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25\). This is a Geometry and Trigonometry question about Circles, at a medium difficulty level. You are asked to write the equation of a circle given its center and one point on the circle.

Core Concepts

  • The standard (center-radius) form of a circle's equation is \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), where \((h, k)\) is the center and \(r\) is the radius.
  • Notice the minus signs inside the parentheses: the coordinates of the center get subtracted. So a center coordinate of \(-4\) becomes \((x - (-4)) = (x + 4)\).
  • The distance between two points \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\) is \(\sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}\). The radius is the distance from the center to any point on the circle, so the squared radius \(r^2\) equals \((x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Identify the center: \((h, k) = (-4, 1)\), so \(h = -4\) and \(k = 1\).
  • Plug the center into the standard form: \((x - (-4))^2 + (y - 1)^2 = r^2\), which simplifies to \((x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = r^2\).
  • Find \(r^2\) using the center \((-4, 1)\) and the point on the circle \((-8, 4)\): \[r^2 = (-8 - (-4))^2 + (4 - 1)^2\]
  • Simplify inside each parenthesis: \[r^2 = (-4)^2 + (3)^2 = 16 + 9 = 25\]
  • Substitute \(r^2 = 25\): \[(x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25\]

Why Each Answer

  • A. \((x - 4)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 5\) — Wrong (sign error and radius error). It uses the center signs backwards (treating the center as \((4, -1)\)) and uses \(r^2 = 5\) instead of \(25\).
  • B. \((x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25\) — Correct. The signs correctly encode the center \((-4, 1)\), and \(r^2 = 25\).
  • C. \((x - 4)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 25\) — Wrong (sign error). The radius is right, but the center signs are flipped, placing the center at \((4, -1)\) instead of \((-4, 1)\).
  • D. \((x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 5\) — Wrong (radius error). The center is encoded correctly, but it uses \(r^2 = 5\); this is the trap of confusing the radius \(r\) with \(r^2\), or forgetting to square the distance result.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
Read the center signs carefully: a negative coordinate flips to a plus inside the equation. Then remember the equation stores \(r^2\), not \(r\) — compute the squared distance and place that number on the right side directly (no extra square root needed). Quick check: the squared distance \(16 + 9 = 25\) is already \(r^2\), so it goes straight into the equation.
questions.question_text: A circle in the \(xy\)-plane has its center at \((-4, 1)\) and the point \((-8, 4)\) lies on the circle. Which equation represents this circle?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot The correct value is \(c = 121\). This is a hard Geometry and Trigonometry item testing lines, angles, and triangles — specifically the angle relationships formed when a transversal crosses two parallel lines.

Core Concepts When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, same-side interior (co-interior) angles are supplementary, meaning they add to \(180^\circ\). Two angles that form a straight line (a linear pair) are also supplementary. In this figure \(a^\circ\) sits at the intersection with line \(r\) and \(b^\circ\), \(c^\circ\) sit at the intersection with line \(s\); \(a\) and \(b\) are the co-interior pair, while \(b\) and \(c\) form a linear pair along line \(s\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown Because \(a\) and \(b\) are co-interior angles between the parallel lines, \(a + b = 180\). Substitute the given expressions: \[\left(4k + 57\right) + \left(\frac{k}{4} + 55\right) = 180.\] Combine like terms: \[4k + \frac{k}{4} + 112 = 180 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{17k}{4} = 68 \;\Rightarrow\; k = 16.\] Then \[a = 4(16) + 57 = 121, \qquad b = \frac{16}{4} + 55 = 59.\] Since \(b\) and \(c\) form a linear pair, \(c = 180 - b = 180 - 59 = 121\).

Why Each Answer The value \(c = 121\) is correct because it is the supplement of \(b = 59\) and equals \(a\) (corresponding-style relationship across the parallels). A common trap answer is \(59\), which is \(b\) itself — chosen if you forget the final linear-pair step. Another trap is \(16\), which is just \(k\) and not an angle measure. A value like \(64\) comes from computing only \(4k\) and dropping the constant. Only \(121\) satisfies every relationship in the figure.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway With parallel lines and a transversal, every angle is either equal to a given angle or its supplement. Find one angle, then \(180 - \text{that}\) gives the rest. Here, once you get \(b = 59\), the answer \(c = 180 - 59 = 121\) follows in one step.
questions.question_text: In the figure, lines \(r\) and \(s\) are parallel and line \(t\) intersects both lines. If \(a = 4k + 57\) and \(b = \frac{k}{4} + 55\), what is the value of \(c\)?

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is A (Infinitely many). This is an Algebra question testing Systems of two linear equations in two variables, at an easy difficulty. We are given two linear equations and asked how many solution pairs \((x, y)\) satisfy both at once.

Core Concepts

  • A solution to a system of two linear equations is any point \((x, y)\) that makes BOTH equations true at the same time. Graphically, each linear equation is a straight line, and a solution is a point where the lines meet.
  • There are exactly three possibilities for two lines: they cross at one point (exactly one solution), they are parallel and never touch (zero solutions), or they are the same line drawn twice (infinitely many solutions). Two distinct lines can never cross at exactly two points, so "exactly two" is never possible for linear systems.
  • A quick test: if you can multiply one whole equation by a single number and turn it into the other equation, the two equations describe the identical line, which means infinitely many solutions.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Start with the first equation: \(0.5x + 1.2y = 9\).
  • Multiply every term on both sides by \(3\): \[3(0.5x) + 3(1.2y) = 3(9)\]
  • Carry out each multiplication: \(3 \times 0.5 = 1.5\), \(3 \times 1.2 = 3.6\), and \(3 \times 9 = 27\).
  • This gives \(1.5x + 3.6y = 27\), which is exactly the second equation.
  • Because the second equation is just the first equation scaled by \(3\), both equations represent the very same line.
  • Every point on that line satisfies both equations, so there are infinitely many solutions.

Why Each Answer

  • A. Infinitely many — Correct. The two equations are scalar multiples of each other (one is \(3\) times the other), so they are the same line and share every point.
  • B. Exactly two — Trap: Conceptual Impossibility. Two straight lines can intersect at most once unless they are identical; "exactly two" can never happen for a linear system.
  • C. Exactly one — Trap: Assumes Distinct Intersecting Lines. This would be right only if the lines had different slopes and crossed at a single point, but here the equations are identical.
  • D. Zero — Trap: Confuses Identical with Parallel. Zero solutions requires parallel lines (same slope, different constant). Here the constant also matches after scaling, so the lines coincide rather than run parallel.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When two linear equations look proportional, divide the coefficients pairwise: \(\frac{1.5}{0.5} = 3\), \(\frac{3.6}{1.2} = 3\), and \(\frac{27}{9} = 3\). When all three ratios match, it is one line drawn twice, giving infinitely many solutions. If only the \(x\) and \(y\) ratios match but the constant ratio differs, the lines are parallel and there are zero solutions.
questions.question_text:
\(0.5x + 1.2y = 9\)
\(1.5x + 3.6y = 27\)
How many solutions does the given system of equations have?

questions.skill: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B) \(89\). This is a Problem-Solving and Data Analysis question testing One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread. Difficulty: medium. The task is to combine two group means into one overall mean.

Core Concepts

  • The mean (average) of a set of values is the sum of all the values divided by how many values there are: \(\text{mean}=\dfrac{\text{sum of values}}{\text{number of values}}\).
  • If you know a group's mean and its size, you can recover the group's total: \(\text{sum}=\text{mean}\times\text{number of values}\).
  • A weighted average combines two or more groups by adding all their totals and dividing by the combined count. You cannot simply average the two means (\(87\) and \(93\)) because the groups have different sizes.

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Step 1 — Total height of the Kerguelen group: \(380\) penguins with mean \(87\) cm give \(380\times 87=33060\) cm.
  • Step 2 — Total height of the Falkland group: \(190\) penguins with mean \(93\) cm give \(190\times 93=17670\) cm.
  • Step 3 — Combined total height: \(33060+17670=50730\) cm.
  • Step 4 — Combined count: \(380+190=570\) penguins.
  • Step 5 — Overall mean: \[\text{Mean}=\frac{50730}{570}=89\text{ centimeters}.\]

Why Each Answer

  • B) \(89\) — Correct. The weighted average \(\frac{50730}{570}=89\) cm correctly accounts for the larger Kerguelen group pulling the mean closer to \(87\) than to \(93\).
  • A) \(91\) — Incorrect (Weighting reversed). This pulls toward \(93\), which would only happen if the Falkland group were the larger one. The bigger group is actually Kerguelen at \(87\) cm.
  • C) \(90\) — Incorrect (Simple average trap). This is the plain average of the two means, \(\frac{87+93}{2}=90\), which ignores that the groups have unequal sizes.
  • D) \(88\) — Incorrect (Miscalculation). This underweights the Falkland group; the true mean sits at \(89\), one centimeter higher.

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
For two-group mean problems, shortcut by factoring out the common size. Here \(380=2\times190\) and \(570=3\times190\), so \(\text{Mean}=\frac{2(87)+1(93)}{3}=\frac{267}{3}=89\). Mental trigger: the combined mean always lands closer to the mean of the larger group, so since Kerguelen (\(87\)) is twice as big, expect an answer nearer \(87\) than \(93\).
questions.question_text: For a study, a research team measured the heights of \(380\) king penguins from the Kerguelen Islands and \(190\) king penguins from the Falkland Islands. The research team determined that the mean height of the \(380\) king penguins from the Kerguelen Islands was \(87 \text{ centimeters}\) and the mean height of the \(190\) king penguins from the Falkland Islands was \(93 \text{ centimeters}\). What was the mean height, in centimeters, of all \(570\) king penguins the research team measured for this study?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot The correct answer is D, \(y = 6(1.55)^x + 18\). This is a Problem-Solving and Data Analysis item on the skill Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots, rated hard. The task is to pick the exponential equation that best models the plotted points.

Core Concepts An exponential model written as \(y = ab^x + c\) has three controlling features. The constant \(c\) is the horizontal asymptote: as \(x\) decreases, \(b^x\) shrinks toward \(0\), so \(y\) levels off at \(y = c\). The value at \(x = 0\) is the y-intercept: \(y = ab^0 + c = a + c\). The base \(b\) controls how fast the curve rises; here every option that grows uses \(b = 1.55\).

Step-by-Step Breakdown Read the figure. On the left the points flatten out along a horizontal line just below \(20\), at about \(y = 18\); that is the asymptote, so \(c = 18\). Near the y-axis the points sit at about \(y = 24\), so the y-intercept is roughly \(24\), giving \(a + c \approx 24\) and therefore \(a \approx 6\). Check a point on the right: at \(x = 4\) the data is near \(y = 50\). Testing option D, \(y = 6(1.55)^4 + 18 \approx 6(5.77) + 18 \approx 52.6\), which lands right beside the plotted point. All three features match option D.

Why Each Answer D is correct: asymptote \(18\), y-intercept \(6 + 18 = 24\), and it tracks the upper points. A, \(y = 24(1.55)^x\), has asymptote \(y = 0\) (factual error: the data never falls toward \(0\)). B, \(y = 24(1.55)^x + 18\), has the right asymptote but a y-intercept of \(24 + 18 = 42\), far above the data (wrong leading coefficient). C, \(y = (1.55)^x + 23\), has asymptote \(y = 23\), above where the left-hand points settle, and a y-intercept of only \(24\) that then grows too slowly (asymptote/coefficient confusion).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway For \(y = ab^x + c\), read two things straight off the graph first: the flat left tail gives \(c\), and the height at \(x = 0\) minus that tail gives \(a\). Those two checks alone usually eliminate every distractor.
questions.question_text: Which of the following equations is the most appropriate model for the data shown in the scatterplot?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is B, \(\frac{9qt}{q-5t}\). This is an Advanced Math question testing the skill of creating Equivalent expressions by isolating a variable through factoring. Difficulty: hard.

Core Concepts

  • Isolating a variable: To solve for one variable in a literal equation, gather every term containing that variable on one side and everything else on the other side.
  • Common factor: If each term shares a number or letter, you may divide the whole equation by it. Here every term has a factor of \(2r\) (since \(18=2\cdot 9\), \(2\) is explicit, and \(10=2\cdot 5\), and each term contains \(r\)).
  • Factoring out a variable: \(qs - 5st = s(q-5t)\); pulling the common \(s\) outside the parentheses lets you divide it away.
  • Why the denominator is safe: We are told \(\frac{q}{t}>5\) with \(q,r,s,t\) positive, so \(q>5t\) and \(q-5t>0\). Dividing by \(q-5t\) is therefore legitimate (no division by zero).

Step-by-Step Breakdown

  • Start with the equation: \[18qrt - 2qrs + 10rst = 0\]
  • Every term contains the factor \(2r\). Divide both sides by \(2r\) (allowed because \(r\) is positive, hence nonzero): \[9qt - qs + 5st = 0\]
  • Move the two terms that contain \(s\) to the right side to keep them together: \[9qt = qs - 5st\]
  • Factor \(s\) out of the right-hand side: \[9qt = s(q - 5t)\]
  • Divide both sides by \((q-5t)\), which is positive as shown above: \[s = \frac{9qt}{q - 5t}\]

Why Each Answer

  • A. \(\frac{-9qt}{q-5t}\): Sign error. This results from moving \(9qt\) incorrectly or factoring \(-s\) instead of \(s\). Since \(q\), \(t\), and \(q-5t\) are all positive, this expression is negative, but \(s\) is positive, so it cannot be correct.
  • B. \(\frac{9qt}{q-5t}\) (correct): Matches the isolation above and is positive, consistent with \(s\) being positive.
  • C. \(18qrt\): Out of Scope. This is simply the first term of the original equation, not the result of solving for \(s\); it still contains \(s\)-free structure and the variable \(r\), which should have canceled.
  • D. \(\frac{2qt}{q-5t}\): Arithmetic trap. The coefficient should be \(9\) (from \(18/2\)), not \(2\); this comes from mishandling the division by \(2r\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway
When an equation has a shared numeric and variable factor in every term, divide it out first to shrink the numbers before isolating. Then group the target variable's terms and factor. A quick sanity check: the answer for a positive quantity must come out positive, which instantly rules out the negative choice A.
questions.question_text:
\(18qrt - 2qrs + 10rst = 0\)
In the given equation, \(q, r, s\), and \(t\) are positive, and \(\frac{q}{t}\) is greater than \(5\). Which expression is equivalent to \(s\)?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot The correct answer is B. This is an easy Algebra item on linear inequalities in two variables, testing how a strict one-variable inequality \(y \gt -36\) is represented as a shaded region in the coordinate plane.

Core Concepts A linear inequality of the form \(y \gt k\) is graphed in two steps. First, the boundary line is the equation \(y = k\) — here \(y = -36\), a horizontal line. Second, the inequality symbol decides two things: whether the boundary is dashed or solid, and which side is shaded. A strict symbol (\(\lt\) or \(\gt\)) means points on the line are NOT solutions, so the boundary is dashed. A non-strict symbol (\(\le\) or \(\ge\)) includes the line, so the boundary is solid. For \(y \gt k\), solutions have a \(y\)-value larger than \(k\), so you shade above the line.

Step-by-Step Breakdown Step 1: Identify the boundary. The inequality \(y \gt -36\) has boundary line \(y = -36\), a horizontal line crossing the \(y\)-axis at \(-36\). Step 2: Dashed or solid? The symbol is \(\gt\) (strictly greater than), so the line is dashed. Step 3: Which side? Because \(y\) must be greater than \(-36\), shade the region above the line. Step 4: Match to a graph. The correct panel must show a dashed horizontal line at \(y = -36\) with everything above it shaded — that is Graph B.

Why Each Answer Graph B is correct: dashed boundary at \(y = -36\) with the region above shaded, exactly representing \(y \gt -36\). Graph A is wrong (wrong side): it uses the correct dashed line at \(y = -36\) but shades below it, which represents \(y \lt -36\). Graph C is wrong (boundary type): it shades the correct region above \(y = -36\) but draws a solid line, which represents \(y \ge -36\) and wrongly includes the boundary. Graph D is wrong (solid line and wrong side): a solid boundary with shading below represents \(y \le -36\).

Pro-Tip & Takeaway Read the symbol as two instructions at once: the line under the symbol (\(\lt\) vs \(\le\)) tells you dashed-versus-solid, and the direction (\(\gt\) points up to "above") tells you which way to shade. Strict means dashed; "greater" means up.
questions.question_text:
\(y > -36\)
Which shaded region represents the solutions to the given inequality?

questions.explanation:
Question Snapshot
The correct answer is D, \(15\). This is an Algebra question testing Linear equations in one variable, rated easy. The goal is to find the value of the whole expression \(5 - 2x\), not the value of \(x\) by itself.

Core Concepts

  • An equation says two expressions are equal. You may add or subtract the same quantity from both sides and the equality still holds.
  • A repeated chunk of an equation can be treated as a single block. Here \(5 - 2x\) shows up on both sides, so we can give it one name and work with that name.
